content: ecades after a 1992 divorce, a husband sought the division of the former family home. The wife claimed a share exceeding 50% due to her higher financial contribution at the time of purchase. The Court clarified that assets bought under the legal community regime are subject to the principle of "community without shares," making unequal contributions irrelevant to ownership titles. Furthermore, it established that if an asset is assigned exclusively to the spouse holding a right of habitation, that right is extinguished by confusion, and the property must be valued at its full market price for the final settlement.
